chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Zayd narrated from Ja‘far ibn Muhammad, from his father عليه السلام, who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام used to say concerning a stray animal that a man finds and intends to take a reward for it, then it perishes: "He is liable for it. But if he did not intend to take a reward for it and it perished, then there is no liability upon him."

key_terms.جُعْلًا: a reward or compensation for returning the item
key_terms.ضَامِنٌ: legally liable to compensate for the loss
key_terms.ضَمَانَ: financial liability or responsibility for compensation
key_terms.ٱلضَّالَّةِ: lost property or a stray animal that has gone missing from its owner

ai.seo_question: Is a person liable if a found stray animal dies while in his possession?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about liability for found stray property or animals. If the finder takes possession with the intention of receiving compensation, he is liable if it perishes; but if he did not intend compensation, then he is not liable. The ruling highlights the legal effect of intention in matters involving the property rights of others.
